description: Use this when the user asks whether a DNS change has landed, wants a DNS record looked up, or wants to verify a record they just published — or whenever answering needs the live value of a record. Reads the record from the domain's OWN nameservers (cache-free) and from two public caching resolvers. `kind` is one of spf|dmarc|txt|mx|cname|a|aaaa — pass the kind, not a query name: `dmarc` reads TXT at _dmarc.<domain> and `spf` reads apex TXT, each filtered to the matching record. `host` prepends a label (txt, cname, a and aaaa only). Pass `expected_value` when checking an edit. Relay `verdict`: done (the nameservers serve it and both caches agree), wait (served, caches catching up — check again after check_again_after_seconds), edit (the domain's nameservers do not serve it; `found_at` names where the value was seen instead, if anywhere). not_registered: true means the domain does not exist (usually a typo). An error starting cant_tell is a lookup fault, never evidence the record is missing. Two resolvers is the whole sample, so never describe this as worldwide or as propagation coverage.

domain.description: The domain to check, e.g. example.com. Bare registrable names and subdomains both work; scheme, path or port do not belong here. Unicode names are accepted and normalized to punycode.
domain.title: Domain

expected_value.description: Optional: the exact value just published (e.g. the DMARC record text, a verification token, '10 mx.example.com'). Given it, the verdict tests for that value and an 'edit' also checks the names a misplaced edit usually lands on (found_at).
expected_value.title: Expected Value

host.description: Optional label to prepend to the domain (e.g. 'mail' to check mail.<domain>) — honored for txt, cname, a and aaaa only; spf, dmarc and mx derive their own query name.
host.title: Host

kind.description: Which record to read; the right query is derived from it — 'dmarc' reads TXT at _dmarc.<domain> filtered to v=DMARC1, 'spf' reads the apex TXT filtered to v=spf1, so don't prefix the domain yourself.
kind.title: Kind

name: check_record
title: Look Up DNS Record
